title: Inference scenario microdeck: ops probe
content:
Purpose:
- Tiny slide set + speaker notes to help SEs and sellers run short technical conversations that end in a pilot ask. Focus = 6–12 minute scenario walkthroughs rather than long demos.

Audience / personas:
- Platform Architect: cares about routing, SLAs, infra isolation (Dedicated/Private).
- Integration Engineer: needs APIs, SDKs, latency & cost numbers to evaluate tradeoffs.
- Product PM (pilot owner): wants outcomes, pilot success criteria, data residency.

High-level thesis:
- Customers decide on inference based on three axes: predictability (SLA), unit economics (cost/1k tokens or embedding query), and control (private vs hosted). This microdeck equips reps to map a customer quickly to a single pilot configuration.

One-slide play (#1): "Latency-first customer (customer-chat)"
- Scenario: Large consumer chat app, 95th pct latency target = 200ms, bursty traffic, need streaming responses.
- Quick ask: 2-week pilot on Dedicated with 1 reserved pool + ingest 50k daily sample messages.
- Key talking points: streaming + KV caching to hit tail latency; autoscale buffers for sudden bursts; routing policy to fallback to cheaper model if capacity strained but keep quality baseline.
- Quick numbers to quote (placeholder, replace with bench): P50 ~40–80ms, P95 ~120–220ms (depending on seq len), cost estimate: $X / 1M tokens on Dedicated baseline, +Y% for streaming CPU overhead.

One-slide play (#2): "Regulated enterprise (evidence summarization)"
- Scenario: Financial firm requires VPC-based deployment, audit logs, KMS/HSM integration. Not tolerant of external network egress.
- Quick ask: Private deployment PoC (VPC) for 30 days with audit retention and small on-prem orchestrator.
- Talking points: private control plane, support for customer KMS, on-prem option for air-gapped workflows, can mirror route to hosted for non-sensitive workloads to reduce TCO.
- Risks & mitigations: sync windows for model updates (schedule outside trading hours), pre-approved list of model variants, signed SLA addendum.

One-slide play (#3): "Cost-sensitive embeddings for semantic search"
- Scenario: Mid-market search product, embedding throughput ~1M vectors/month, wants deterministic cost per query.
- Quick ask: 30-day Optimize consult + pilot to configure quantization + batching + cache for embedding reuse.
- Talking points: recommend quantized candidate model, cheap CPU-hosted encoding for short inputs, cache strategy for near-duplicate docs; expected savings 30–60% vs naive host.

Objection handling (rapid bullets):
- "What if we lose accuracy with quantization?" -> show example A/B: precision@10 delta < 3% for typical ecom dataset, fallback to full-float for failover queries.
- "Can Redwood guarantee latency at scale?" -> SLA for Dedicated, example customer case study (anonymized) who sustained 10k reqs/s with <250ms p95 using autoscale + batching controls.
- "We need data residency" -> Private + VPC + deployable on-prem; refer to integration doc (confluence id linked).

Pilot success criteria (proposed):
- Latency: p95 under target (set per-customer).
- Cost: cost/token within agreed threshold vs baseline.
- Functionality: feature parity on all critical API calls and webhooks.
- Ops: audit events enabled and access control validated.

Slide order / deck outline (6 slides):
1) Title + purpose + 1-sentence outcome
2) Decision axes diagram (predictability / cost / control) + mapping to Redwood products
3) Play A: latency-first (bullets + 2 lines of numbers)
4) Play B: regulated/private (bullets + checklist)
5) Play C: cost-sensitive embeddings (bullets + expected savings table)
6) Pilot ask + checklist + next steps + quick script

Quick script (30s / 90s variants):
- 30s: "We help you hit [latency/cost/regulatory] goals without rebuilding inference. Start with a two-week pilot on Dedicated/Private so you can measure latency and cost on your real traffic—if it’s not a fit we can roll back the test easily."
- 90s: expanded: include routing/fallback, KV caching, and expected MVE (minimum viable economics) numbers.

Example pilot checklist (for SEs):
- ingest sample workload (anonymized) -- DONE
- instrument token-level metrics + traces -- TODO
- enable prefix caching config -- TODO
- agree on SLA & rollback criteria -- TODO
- schedule 30-min kickoff with infra contact -- TODO

Open questions / TODOs:
- Replace placeholders with real bench numbers from infra/serving runtime (ask: Marina for latest p95 matrix).
- Add one-line anonymized customer case for Dedicated throughput.
- Validate quantization accuracy numbers on legal-doc dataset (Devon to run).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the deck to 6 slides; sellers hate decks longer than a minute.
- Include a single appendix slide with links to deeper docs and the SLA template.
- Prototype one-page PDF cheat sheet that can be attached to pilot emails.

Appendix (links to include on final slide):
- Confluence: deployment checklist
- GitHub: quickstart scripts for private deploy
- Jira: pilot request template (GTMSPR-87)

Speaker cues:
- Slide 2: point at decision axes, ask "Which of these three is top for you?" and map on the fly.
- Slides 3–5: keep to 2–3 bullets each + one number.

Version notes:
- v0.1 (this file) = ops-probe draft for internal playtest.
- v0.2 = after bench numbers & anonymized case study.

End of microdeck.
